Council approves $4.2 million for the harbour ferry

By Aisha Doucette · {{DATE}} · Politics

Halifax regional council voted 12 to 4 on Tuesday to spend $4.2 million on two electric ferries for the harbour crossing. The vessels they replace were built in 1986 and have missed 140 sailings this year for repairs.

The new ferries will carry 200 passengers each and charge overnight at the Alderney terminal. Delivery is expected in two years. Councillors who voted against the plan asked for the money to go to bus service in the suburbs instead.

The transit director told council the ferries carry 1.8 million passengers a year and that the repair budget for the old vessels has doubled since 2022.
